Coverage

203 services: 159 Concepts and 44 SOW templates. The canvas has 201 services; CW00 and X01 were also checked in the SOW catalog.

75 connection records: their descriptions, data directions, prerequisites and attached flow references.

190 distinct original URLs: 188 returned readable page content. The Commerce overview has a verified replacement address. The security PDF retrieval remains unresolved.

The source register also records 85 additional evidence URLs used in the findings and proposed corrections.

Keep Concept. It can continue to identify a partner-scoped service idea. The correction is to make the supporting evidence precise and to distinguish documented product behavior from the partner's delivery plan. Adobe documentation does not validate the generator's hours, price, quantities or promised business lift.

The Workspace projects and dashboards example

CJ04 is a citation-fit problem. Its current quick-start link establishes that Analysis Workspace is used for analysis. The Create Projects page directly explains building projects from panels, visualizations and components, and is a much better primary citation.

Keep the service and Concept label. Define the delivery as browser-based Analysis Workspace projects. If the partner also intends to deliver executive mobile dashboards, explicitly add mobile scorecards to scope and cite Create and share scorecards. A dashboard label alone should not silently commit the partner to both formats.

A05Governance and change managementEdge Delivery Services | SOW templatePartial supportHigh

Adobe documents agents for AEM as a Cloud Service and Edge Delivery Services and supports automated brand checks. This service commits to configured checks without confirming the client's Governance Agent access, policy setup and supported checking workflow.

What is supported

Brand-policy checks through available AEM agent capabilities.

Gap

  • The current assumptions do not condition automated checks on tenant access or the supported workflow for the client's authoring route.
  • Brand-policy import and check configuration need their own implementation reference.

Exact recommended correction

Add: "Before committing to configured automated checks, confirm Governance Agent access and the supported workflow for the Client's AEM or Edge Delivery authoring route; configure the agreed brand policy and validate checks on the agreed templates. If that capability is unavailable, scope a partner-run standards, review and approval process and revise the automated-check deliverable and acceptance criteria before delivery." Add Overview of Agents in AEM and How to Import a Brand Policy.

Current citations

  • S076: Governance Agent Overview | Adobe Experience Manager

Recommended citations

  • S076: Governance Agent Overview | Adobe Experience Manager
  • S216: Overview of Agents in AEM | Adobe Experience Manager
  • S214: How to Import A Brand Policy | Adobe Experience Manager

Evidence checked

  • S076: Governance Agent Overview | Adobe Experience Manager
    Section: Brand Governance
  • S216: Overview of Agents in AEM | Adobe Experience Manager
    Section: Accessing Agents; Limitations
  • S214: How to Import A Brand Policy | Adobe Experience Manager

Verification notes

Adobe's general agent overview explicitly includes both AEM as a Cloud Service and Edge Delivery Services and describes trial, Try Before You Buy and Agentic SKU access. It does not establish every agent-specific authoring route. Do not impose a blanket AEM Cloud authoring requirement or infer that an EDS license alone provides agent access. Organizational change management and training remain partner work.

Original wording reviewed
Scope

Set the design-system and component standards every team follows; turn the Client's brand and content rules into governance checks in AEM; define roles, approvals and the publishing process; and run the change program (training, playbooks, office hours) for the authoring teams.

Basis

One site: design-system standards, content governance, and the change program for the teams who will author and publish.

Deliverable

Design-system standards, configured governance checks, the roles and approvals model, training materials and a change plan.

Acceptance

The authoring teams publish through the agreed process, and the governance checks run on the agreed templates.

Assumptions

The Client names a content owner and the teams in scope. Hours scale with the number of teams and templates.

Exclusions

Writing the content, the build, and organizational design beyond the authoring teams.

XA03Journey Optimizer Decisioning and recommendationsReal-Time CDP + Journey Optimizer | ConceptPartial supportHigh

The blueprint supports next-best-offer logic but mixes current Decisioning with legacy Decision Management terminology and placements. Behavioral recommendations are a distinct pattern on another page. The capabilities exist; the citation and implementation vocabulary need separation.

What is supported

Offer eligibility and ranking on profile/audience data; behavioral recommendation has separate official support.

Gap

  • The sole link does not substantiate the behavioral-recommendation implementation.
  • “Placements in Journey Optimizer Decisioning” conflates the current framework with legacy Decision Management terminology.

Exact recommended correction

Replace the lead citation with Get started with Decisioning and add Behavioral recommendation. Replace scope with: “Configure decision items and collections, eligibility rules, ranking methods, selection strategies and decision policies using RTCDP audiences and attributes. Where included, configure behavioral recommendation strategies and validate the required catalog and behavioral signals.” Keep legacy placements only in explicitly scoped Decision Management work.

A01Implement AEM Sites on Edge DeliveryEdge Delivery Services | SOW templatePartial supportMedium

The EDS overview substantiates the site implementation but not the additional Brand Visibility routing configuration in its scope.

What is supported

EDS architecture and implementation approach.

Gap

  • Brand Visibility edge-routing eligibility requires a separate product reference.

Exact recommended correction

Keep the EDS overview and add Optimize at Edge plus the AEM managed-CDN setup. Retain the existing condition that the actual outer CDN must qualify and be detected for the self-service route; otherwise use the applicable CDN route.

Current citations

  • S089: Edge Delivery Services Overview | Adobe Experience Manager

Recommended citations

  • S089: Edge Delivery Services Overview | Adobe Experience Manager
  • S050: Optimize at Edge | Adobe Brand Visibility
  • S049: Optimize at Edge - AEM Cloud Service Managed CDN (Fastly) | Adobe Brand Visibility

Evidence checked

  • S089: Edge Delivery Services Overview | Adobe Experience Manager
    Section: How does it work; Authoring
  • S050: Optimize at Edge | Adobe Brand Visibility
    Section: CDN onboarding
  • S049: Optimize at Edge - AEM Cloud Service Managed CDN (Fastly) | Adobe Brand Visibility
    Section: Prerequisites; configure routing
Original wording reviewed
Scope

Turn Brand Visibility findings and the Client's search strategy into the site plan and information architecture; design and build the block library and page templates on Edge Delivery; set up authoring, the CDN route (Adobe's managed CDN or the Client's own, confirmed in discovery) and the agreed integrations; build the agreed pages; and set up Brand Visibility's Optimize at Edge routing on that CDN.

Basis

One site on Edge Delivery Services: the site plan from the SEO and AI strategy, a block library and page templates, build and integrations for the agreed page set.

Deliverable

A working Edge Delivery site with templates and blocks, configured authoring, CDN route and integrations, Brand Visibility's edge routing verified, and a build record.

Acceptance

The agreed pages render on Edge Delivery, meet the agreed performance and quality checks, and the Client accepts the site for migration and launch.

Assumptions

The Client has licensed AEM Sites with Edge Delivery Services and provides brand assets, content owners and approvers. The page set, templates and integrations are confirmed before the build. Hours scale with the number of templates, blocks, pages and integrations. Optimize at Edge serves AI agents an optimized copy at the CDN without changing the pages people see; lasting fixes go into the source content through the authoring and publishing workflow. Routing is self-serve in Brand Visibility on AEM as a Cloud Service's managed Fastly CDN, and this service turns it on there and allows the AdobeEdgeOptimize/1.0 user agent in robots.txt and bot rules; Adobe documents the self-serve route for AEM as a Cloud Service, so it is confirmed for the Edge Delivery site with Adobe. On any other CDN the CDN team adds the rules.

Exclusions

Content migration, launch and hypercare (separate services), custom back-end systems, commerce storefronts, translation and pages outside the agreed set.

A02SEO-safe content migrationEdge Delivery Services | SOW templatePartial supportMedium

The go-live checklist directly supports migration SEO validation, redirects and post-launch checks. It does not describe the content-import part of the service.

What is supported

Migration launch and SEO validation.

Gap

  • Content conversion and import require a complementary source.

Exact recommended correction

Keep Go-Live Checklist and add Importing Content. Retain the existing no-ranking-guarantee qualification; the word "safe" describes the planned controls, not a guaranteed search outcome.

Original wording reviewed
Scope

Map the current site to the new one; migrate the agreed pages into Edge Delivery documents and blocks; carry over or rewrite titles, descriptions, headings and structured data; set up redirects, bulk metadata and sitemaps; run crawl, link and Lighthouse checks before launch.

Basis

One site migration: the agreed pages, redirects, metadata and sitemaps, with crawl and performance checks before launch.

Deliverable

Migrated pages, the redirect map, metadata and sitemap records, and the pre-launch check report.

Acceptance

Every page in the agreed set is migrated, every redirect resolves, and the crawl, link and Lighthouse checks pass the agreed thresholds.

Assumptions

The Client provides access to the current site, its analytics and search data, and reviewers. The build is accepted before migration starts. Hours scale with the number of pages and how much copy is rewritten.

Exclusions

New content, translation, pages outside the agreed set and changes to the site build. Search rankings are not guaranteed.

Scope

Configure the supported ABV bot-data connection and map URLs and hosts; identify AI-referred visits in the existing CJA web data with a derived field on AI referring domains; and align observed AI-referral and conversion measures with existing CJA data.

Basis

One existing CJA environment and reporting workspace, with up to five business measures.

Deliverable

Validated connection, metric definitions and an initial report of AI-agent activity and AI-referred visits and conversions, kept as separate measures.

Acceptance

Bot measures reconcile to ABV and visits/conversions reconcile to the agreed existing web data. Measurement limitations are documented.

Assumptions

The integration is available (Brand Visibility's AI-agent data reaches CJA as an Experience Platform dataset through the Adobe Brand Visibility source, which the Client adds to a CJA connection and data view; Adobe Analytics can feed only Brand Visibility's referral reporting on the Business Impact tab), the Client is on the paid Brand Visibility offer (trial workspaces cannot connect), the CJA integration is enabled for the organization, and CDN log forwarding is live, since the connection reads the CDN log summaries. Client application owners provide access and approve metric definitions. The Client has licensed CJA Select, Prime or Ultimate (derived fields are not included in CJA Foundation).

Exclusions

New CJA implementation, data-collection repair, historical migration, person-level linkage from an AI mention and ongoing monthly reporting.

Scope

Exclusions

This is the one monthly readout. Where Sites Optimizer's monthly fixes are in scope, it includes their search results, and they produce no separate report. Edge fixes chosen here go live only where an edge route is in place; otherwise they are listed for a pilot or as change requests. Findings that need a change to the site itself go to Sites Optimizer's monthly fixes where those are in scope, and otherwise to the Client's web team.

Exclusions

Content production, code changes, outreach, new analytics implementation and duplicate reporting in an integration or separate test package.

Verification notes

Reviewed service scope and associated connection qualifications. Consulting hours, quantities and cadence are partner estimates, not Adobe commitments.

Original wording reviewed
Scope

For the agreed tables: confirm with the Client's data team that change tracking is on for each table, create the relational schemas (a primary key and a version, plus a timestamp for event data), set up the Experience Platform source with change data capture (Data Mirror), map the fields and set the schedule, add the datasets to the CJA connection (the existing connection, or the one Connections, data views and stitching sets up) with their join, and add their fields to the data view.

Basis

Up to five tables from one Snowflake, Google BigQuery or Azure Databricks warehouse, through Data Mirror.

Deliverable

Synced datasets for the agreed tables in the CJA connection and data view, with a mapping record.

Acceptance

Record counts in CJA match the warehouse for an agreed day, and an update and a delete made in the warehouse show in CJA after the next sync.

Assumptions

The Client has CJA Select, Prime or Ultimate (Data Mirror is not in CJA Foundation), and Data Mirror is enabled for the organization. The Client's data team gives the access the source needs (for Google BigQuery, a dataset for temporary tables; for Azure Databricks, a SAS token in the cluster's Spark configuration), allows Adobe's IP addresses where the warehouse needs it and turns on change tracking for each table (each warehouse has its own setting). Mirrored changes count toward the CJA ingestion limit. Other warehouses, such as Amazon Redshift or Azure Synapse Analytics, need separately licensed source connectors without Data Mirror, and a service of their own. On Experience Platform running on AWS, Adobe lists Google BigQuery and Snowflake as sources, not Azure Databricks. When CJA data preparation in Experience Platform is also in this SOW, this service covers only the work that service does not.

Exclusions

Changes to the Client's warehouse or tables (the Client turns on change tracking), licenses, and new CJA connections or data views.

Original wording reviewed
Scope

Activate Sites Optimizer on the production site, connect Google Search Console, set who can deploy fixes and who can prepare code patches, and review the first SEO opportunities (broken backlinks, metadata, structured data, sitemap issues, Core Web Vitals) with the Client to agree what to fix first. Agree the route and owner for each kind of fix (authoring or source documents, code patches, or configuration such as redirects), deploy the first agreed content fixes (with Prime, apply them by hand) and prepare any code patches they need.

Basis

One site: Sites Optimizer connected, roles set, and the first SEO opportunities reviewed with the team.

Deliverable

Configured Sites Optimizer, the roles and approvals model, the route and owner for each kind of fix, and a prioritized list of the first SEO fixes.

Acceptance

The Client can see and approve opportunities, each kind of fix has an agreed route and owner, the first agreed content fixes are in authoring (with Prime, applied by hand), and any code patches for them are with the named developer.

Assumptions

The Client has licensed Sites Optimizer for AEM Sites (Edge Delivery, Cloud Service or Managed Services) and the site is a public production site. Hours scale with the number of sites.

How a fix is deployed depends on its opportunity. With the Ultimate package, approved content fixes go into authoring (on document-authored Edge Delivery sites, into the source documents) for people to review and publish, and Core Web Vitals fixes are prepared as code patches for a named developer who reviews, tests, merges and releases them. Deploying to authoring and preparing code patches each need the user's permission for that action and a fully configured site (Adobe's example is a connected code repository).

Code patches reach the developer as a pull request in the connected repository or as a downloaded patch; Adobe's October 2026 release notes list pull-request submission for Core Web Vitals as Early Access, so the route is confirmed here. On AEM as a Cloud Service sites, deploying broken-backlink redirects through Dispatcher is Early Access, used only where Adobe has enabled it.

With Prime, which identifies and suggests fixes, the first agreed content and configuration fixes are applied by hand and code fixes go to the named developer.

Core Web Vitals come from real-user data (Operational Telemetry, connected during setup if it isn't yet), and Adobe analyzes them only on pages with at least 1,000 page views.

Brand Visibility connects its own Search Console link; one access request to the Client covers both. Access for Adobe's scanner is confirmed here and its IP addresses are allowed in the CDN, firewall or Cloud Manager traffic filters.

Exclusions

The Sites Optimizer license, fixes outside the agreed opportunity types, and changes to systems outside AEM.

SEO opportunity review and code-patch preparation.

Gap

Retain the opportunity index and code-patch references. Add Deploying to Author, the Sites Optimizer package description and the dated release-note sections for pull requests and Dispatcher redirects. Keep the current human publication and developer review responsibilities.

Original wording reviewed
Scope

Each month, review new SEO opportunities in Sites Optimizer, approve or edit the suggested fixes with the content owner, deploy the content fixes to authoring for people to publish, prepare the code patches (such as Core Web Vitals fixes) and hand them to the named developer to review, test, merge and release, and report search traffic and Core Web Vitals movement in the Brand Visibility review.

Basis

One site: each month, review Sites Optimizer's new SEO opportunities, approve the fixes, deploy the content fixes, hand code patches to the developer, and report the results.

Deliverable

Monthly fix log with each fix's route and status, and the month's search results.

Acceptance

The month's agreed content fixes are in authoring, ready for the Client to publish (with Prime, applied by hand), the month's code patches are with the named developer and their status is in the fix log, and the results are reported.

Assumptions

Sites Optimizer is licensed and set up. Hours scale with the number of opportunities and sites. Sites Optimizer finds the opportunities and suggests fixes on its own.

How an approved fix is deployed depends on its opportunity: with the Ultimate package, content fixes go into authoring (on document-authored Edge Delivery sites, into the source documents) and people publish them, and Core Web Vitals fixes are prepared as code patches that the named developer reviews, tests, merges and releases through the existing development workflow.

Code patches arrive as pull requests or downloaded patches, by the route agreed at setup, and either way go through the Client's own review and release process; on AEM as a Cloud Service sites, broken-backlink redirects deploy through Dispatcher only where Adobe has enabled that Early Access feature.

With Prime (identify and suggest only), the partner applies approved content and configuration fixes by hand, and code fixes go to the named developer with Sites Optimizer's recommendation.

These hours cover reviewing and editing the suggestions with the content owner, deploying the content fixes, preparing the code patches and handing them to the developer, and the report; the developer's review, testing, merge and release are outside these hours unless agreed.

These are the month's site fixes in one allowance, and the site fixes Brand Visibility flags (robots.txt rules for AI crawlers, redirects for pages AI agents can't reach) are made by hand in the site's configuration or redirect sheet, within the same allowance.

Exclusions

The license, new content creation (a separate service), the developer's review, testing, merge and release of code patches unless agreed, and development outside AEM.

  • S182: Customer Journey Analytics | Product Description
    Section: Packaging; unlicensed features
    Derived Fields requires Select or higher; CJA does not itself license general Profile or Segmentation services.

Verification notes

Reviewed service scope and associated connection qualifications. Consulting hours, quantities and cadence are partner estimates, not Adobe commitments.

Original wording reviewed
Scope

Define up to five audiences from AI-referred visits and their outcomes in the CJA data view, publish them to Real-Time Customer Profile, and agree with the Client how each audience is used in its existing channels.

Basis

One CJA data view: up to five audiences from AI-referred visitors, published to Real-Time Customer Profile, with an activation plan.

Deliverable

Audience definitions, the published audiences, an activation plan with owners, and the measures to review in the monthly report.

Acceptance

The audiences populate in Real-Time Customer Profile with the agreed definitions, and the Client approves the activation plan.

Assumptions

The Client licenses Real-Time CDP or Journey Optimizer, because CJA audience publishing to Real-Time Customer Profile needs one of them; CJA alone does not license Profile Service. The Client has licensed CJA Select, Prime or Ultimate (derived fields are not included in CJA Foundation). A CJA administrator, who gets the Audience Publishing permission automatically, also has Experience Platform's Manage Profiles permission. The Person ID in the CJA connection is agreed: CJA sends it as each audience member's primary identity, one identity per person. Channel owners confirm identity, consent and the intended use, and take part. Any downstream destination is already configured and licensed in Experience Platform and is activated there after the audience is published. The source datasets don't need to be enabled for Profile. Audiences come from AI-referred visitors in the Client's existing web data, found with a derived field on AI referring domains; the Brand Visibility dataset holds only aggregate AI-agent activity by URL and host, with no personal identifiers, and is not needed for these audiences.

Exclusions

New destinations or channels, campaign production, personalization builds and audience work in other tools.

Original wording reviewed
Scope

For the agreed file feeds in Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, Google Cloud Storage or SFTP: create the schema and dataset, set up the Experience Platform cloud storage source (authentication, files, mapping and schedule), add the dataset to the CJA connection (the existing connection, or the one Connections, data views and stitching sets up) and its fields to the data view, and check the first loads.

Basis

Up to three file feeds from one cloud storage location.

Deliverable

Scheduled dataflows for the agreed feeds, their datasets in the CJA connection and data view, and a mapping record.

Acceptance

The first scheduled loads succeed, and the records in CJA match the source files for an agreed day.

Assumptions

Included with a CJA license (Adobe's product description lets the Client configure non-Adobe sources into CJA). The Client provides the storage location, credentials and delimited files, or JSON or Parquet files already in XDM format, and allows Adobe's IP addresses where needed. CJA Foundation allows one event dataset per connection. On Experience Platform running on AWS, Adobe lists Amazon S3 among these sources; the others are listed for Azure. When CJA data preparation in Experience Platform is also in this SOW, this service covers only the work that service does not.

Exclusions

Building the Client's exports into storage, new CJA connections or data views, and file cleanup.

    C07CDN readiness and routing where requiredBrand Visibility + Adobe Commerce | SOW templateDirect supportNone

    The source describes the CDN and bot-access work at the heart of this service. Its scope appropriately conditions provider-specific routing on the actual customer setup.

    What is supported

    Outer-CDN readiness and routing.

    Gap

    No material citation gap recorded.

    Exact recommended correction

    Keep the current service and citation.

    Current citations

    • S050: Optimize at Edge | Adobe Brand Visibility

    Recommended citations

    No replacement required.

    Evidence checked

    • S050: Optimize at Edge | Adobe Brand Visibility
      Section: Requirements for your IT/CDN team; supported providers

    Verification notes

    Use the provider-specific guide linked from this page during delivery. The existing Commerce Fastly qualification avoids assuming AEM self-service eligibility.

    Original wording reviewed
    Scope

    Confirm how the store serves pages to AI agents and search engines and which CDN sits closest to visitors, since routing goes on that outer CDN. Prepare and test the Optimize at Edge routing rules for that CDN (Adobe's guides cover Fastly, Akamai, Cloudflare, CloudFront, Azure Front Door and Apache) and have the Client's CDN team, or the partner with delegated access, apply them in the agreed change window; allow Adobe's edge-optimization user agent through robots.txt and any firewall or bot-manager rules, keep the cache for AI agents separate, test failover to the origin and rollback, and verify one page before the first optimization goes live through the route.

    Basis

    One Adobe Commerce store and its outer CDN: Optimize at Edge routing for AI agents, verified on one page.

    Deliverable

    The documented CDN topology and routing, the configured rules, the one-page verification, the rollback steps and the handoff of the verified route for the first edge deployment.

    Acceptance

    An approved optimization reaches AI agents through the Client's outer CDN on the verification page, people and search bots still get the origin page, rollback is tested, and the Client's hosting owner accepts the configuration.

    Assumptions

    The CDN topology, the routing owner and a change window are confirmed in week one: the partner prepares and tests the rules, the Client's CDN team (or the partner, with delegated access) applies them, and the hosting owner approves. Adobe documents self-serve routing only for AEM as a Cloud Service sites on Adobe's managed Fastly CDN and documents no edge route for Adobe Commerce on cloud infrastructure, so this plan puts the routing rules on the outer CDN (for a store served straight from Commerce's Fastly service, that service) and the partner confirms the route and effort with Adobe (abv-at-edge@adobe.com) before the change window. Where an existing setup is confirmed ready, this service confirms and verifies it.

    Exclusions

    CDN migration or new CDN contracts, replatforming, the optimizations deployed through the route (separate services) and store code changes.

    The checklist and handoff guide substantiate the bounded implementation and release controls.

    What is supported

    Gap

    • S036: Live Chat and Meeting Booking Overview | Adobe Brand Concierge

    Evidence checked

    • S039: Your Pre-Go-Live Checklist and Rollout Plan | Adobe Brand Concierge
      Section: Pre-go-live checklist; phased rollout
      Covers content readiness, guardrails, response testing, stakeholder signoff and staged rollout.
    • S036: Live Chat and Meeting Booking Overview | Adobe Brand Concierge
      Section: Prerequisites; setup path; data retention
      Documents live chat, meeting booking, Marketo dependencies and 30-day chat retention.

    Verification notes

    Reviewed complete record including scope, deliverables, acceptance, assumptions, size bands, neutral wording and associated connection qualifications. Partner hours and quantities are estimates, not Adobe commitments. Existing assumptions appropriately reserve financial content approval for the Client and exclude undocumented contact-center integrations.

    Original wording reviewed
    Scope

    Set up the Brand Concierge experience for the agreed banking or insurance products: connect and curate the approved content sources, design the conversations and guardrails for the agreed questions, configure the brand voice and the required disclosures, set up the handoff (live chat, meeting booking or both) routed to one Client-designated team, build, with the Client's reviewers, the golden-answer test set (including the priority discovery questions from the Brand Visibility program) and the refusal and escalation scenarios, complete Adobe's pre-go-live checks, and launch on the agreed pages in stages.

    Basis

    One Brand Concierge experience: approved content sources, conversation design for the agreed products, one handoff route, testing and launch on the agreed pages. Adobe's Brand Concierge FAQ puts a basic setup at about 3 to 5 days, an advanced implementation at about 2 to 4 weeks and go-live at about 6 to 9 weeks; these hours are a planning assumption for the work around that setup, not yet reconciled with Adobe's figures or an independent delivery estimate.

    Deliverable

    A live Brand Concierge experience on the agreed pages; the source, guardrail and disclosure configuration; the golden-answer test set and results; the refusal and escalation scenarios; the completed pre-go-live checklist; and the launch and rollout record.

    Acceptance

    Client reviewers approve the sampled answers, disclosures and the handoff; the golden-answer set scores at or above the agreed level for correctness, helpfulness and brand fit, and the refusal and escalation scenarios pass; stakeholders sign off the pre-go-live checks; and the experience is live on the agreed pages, rolled out in the agreed stages.

    Assumptions

    The Client has licensed Brand Concierge and supplies the approved content, current product facts, reviewers and the handoff destination; compliance decisions stay with the Client.

    The documented handoff is live chat or meeting booking through Adobe Marketo Qualifier (formerly Sales Qualifier), which needs the representatives added as users in the Adobe Admin Console and at least one representative with a connected calendar (for meeting booking) or set live chat availability (for live chat); a handoff to another chat or contact-center platform is not a documented route and is confirmed with Adobe first.

    Live chat and meeting booking don't need Marketo Engage: round robin and direct-agent routing work without it, and it is needed only for custom routing rules, which pick a team by Marketo attributes, and for writing concierge activities to the Marketo person record. Live chat conversations are kept for 30 days, so the Client confirms its own record-keeping needs.

    The baseline is the anonymous, public-information experience; profile-based answers are not assumed. Hours scale with the number of products, sources, journeys and test conversations.

    These hours cover the partner's work around Adobe's setup: approved sources and reviewers, conversation and disclosure design, the handoff, the golden-answer and refusal tests and the staged rollout.

    Exclusions

    New content, legal or compliance advice, a new chat or appointment platform, ongoing answer review (a separate service) and Coworker Skills.

    "deliverable": "A live Brand Concierge experience on the agreed pages; the source, guardrail and disclosure configuration; both handoff routes, configured and tested; the golden-answer test set and results; the refusal and escalation scenarios; the completed pre-go-live checklist; and the launch and rollout record.",
    "acceptance": "Client reviewers approve the sampled answers, disclosures and both handoff routes; the golden-answer set scores at or above the agreed level for correctness, helpfulness and brand fit, and the refusal and escalation scenarios pass; stakeholders sign off the pre-go-live checks; and the experience is live on the agreed pages, rolled out in the agreed stages."

    L03Automated optimization deployment pilotBrand Visibility + Adobe Commerce | SOW templateDirect supportNone

    The two citations support the edge deployment and its eligible measurement. The existing paid-offer, supported-opportunity, URL-eligibility and rollback qualifications are material and appropriate.

    What is supported

    Eligible deployment pilot and IME readout.

    Gap

    No material citation gap recorded.

    Exact recommended correction

    Keep the current service and citation.

    Current citations

    • S048: Impact Measurement Engine | Adobe Brand Visibility
    • S050: Optimize at Edge | Adobe Brand Visibility

    Recommended citations

    No replacement required.

    Evidence checked

    • S050: Optimize at Edge | Adobe Brand Visibility
      Section: Onboarding; deploy and rollback
    • S048: Impact Measurement Engine | Adobe Brand Visibility
      Section: Eligibility; measurement period

    Verification notes

    The catalog already distinguishes a measurable deployment from all deployed pages and records the conflicting trial limits; no trial capability is certified here.

    Original wording reviewed
    Scope

    Using the agreed Optimize at Edge route, check that each selected page sends a Last-Modified header where the opportunity needs one, then deploy approved changes for one supported opportunity type (such as Recover Content Visibility, Add Table of Contents or Add LLM-friendly Summaries) to 20 to 50 URLs chosen with the High Potential URLs filter, in one deployment; verify rollback; keep those pages unchanged during the measurement period; and run two operator sessions. Review the Impact Measurement Engine's analysis with the Client if Adobe generates one.

    Basis

    One deployment of 20 to 50 eligible URLs on an agreed Optimize at Edge route.

    Deliverable

    Validated deployment pilot, release and rollback checklist, operator handover, and the Impact Measurement Engine's impact analysis when Adobe generates one for the deployment.

    Acceptance

    Approved pilot changes deploy successfully, rollback is verified and the Client accepts release ownership. The impact analysis is reviewed when available; it is not an acceptance condition, because Adobe generates it only for eligible deployments and measures only pages with enough data, using a representative subset of the URLs.

    Assumptions

    The Client has an eligible deployment route (Optimize at Edge routing on the outer CDN: already in place; set up self-serve in Brand Visibility, as part of this pilot, for AEM as a Cloud Service sites on Adobe's managed Fastly CDN (where Implement AEM Sites on Edge Delivery is part of this engagement, it turns the route on); applied by the Client's CDN team; or set up by CDN readiness and routing), access, capacity and approved changes. Where routing covers only some paths, the selected URLs are inside them. Trial workspaces have tighter deployment limits (Adobe's pages give 10 pages, or 50 URLs for trials from April 1, 2026), so the paid offer is assumed. Adobe lists edge auto-optimization as Early Access for select opportunities, so the opportunity type is confirmed for the Client. Adobe generates an impact analysis only for eligible deployments: a supported opportunity type and at least 20 URLs from the High Potential URLs filter in a single deployment. Recover Content Visibility results typically take about two weeks. For content opportunities such as Add LLM-friendly Summaries, Brand Visibility watches the source page's Last-Modified response header: it pauses the optimization for review when the page changes and skips it when the header is missing. A selected page without the header is replaced, or the Client's team adds the header before deployment.

    Exclusions

    Custom connectors, CDN migration, ongoing optimization and pilot work already included in another selected service.

    Scope bands
    {
  "driver": "URLs in each deployment and the number of deployments",
  "small": {
    "qty": "One route; one deployment of fewer than 20 URLs. The pages are optimized, but Adobe's impact analysis is not expected below 20 High Potential URLs",
    "scope": "Using the agreed Optimize at Edge route, check that each selected page sends a Last-Modified header where the opportunity needs one, then deploy approved changes for one supported opportunity type (such as Recover Content Visibility, Add Table of Contents or Add LLM-friendly Summaries) to fewer than 20 URLs, in one deployment; verify rollback; and run one operator session. Adobe's impact analysis is not expected for a deployment of this size.",

  },

  },

Review each Impact Measurement Engine analysis with the Client if Adobe generates one.",
    "deliverable": "Validated deployment pilot, release and rollback checklist, operator handover, and the Impact Measurement Engine's impact analysis when Adobe generates one for each deployment."

      Section: Manual uploads; file format; processing
    Original wording reviewed
    Scope

    For a CDN without an Adobe guide, or logs kept in a log store such as Splunk or Elasticsearch: build and schedule an export that writes the access logs as newline-delimited JSON with the field names and types Adobe specifies, and uploads them to the dated location Brand Visibility provides.

    Basis

    Up to three domains from one CDN without an Adobe guide, or from one log store.

    Deliverable

    A scheduled export, its documentation and one validated day of logs.

    Acceptance

    A day of logs uploads without skipped lines and shows in Brand Visibility's reports after Adobe's daily processing.

    Assumptions

    Each agreed domain is already onboarded in Brand Visibility. The Client's logs contain the fields Adobe requires, and the Client runs the scheduler or serverless function that sends them (Adobe's examples are AWS Lambda and Azure Functions). Adobe processes uploaded logs near the end of each UTC day; malformed lines may be skipped.

    Exclusions

    Changes to the CDN or the log store, and log retention.

    Verification notes

    The PDF retrieval failed with DisabledError; the Trust Center landing page requires sign-in for its library. This is an inability to verify the specific PDF claim, not proof that the feed is absent or that this particular PDF requires an NDA.

    Original wording reviewed
    How

    On AEM as a Cloud Service's managed CDN, Brand Visibility's Optimize at Edge is self-serve when that CDN is the outer CDN (your client's CDN in front needs its own routing). The AI agents Adobe supports (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude) get the optimized version of pages where a fix is deployed; visitors and search bots still get AEM's pages.

    Kind

    native

    Availability

    Not stated by Adobe. Trial limits conflict: one opportunity on up to 10 pages (Optimize at Edge FAQ), or up to 50 URLs for one opportunity type for trials from April 1, 2026 (Quick Start).

    Prereqs
    • Brand Visibility license; users need the Adobe LLM Optimizer Users product profile (trial users: the LLMO Admin IMS group)
    • Site served by the AEM as a Cloud Service managed CDN (Fastly) as the outer CDN; your client's CDN in front needs its own routing
    • Robots.txt and bot rules that let AdobeEdgeOptimize/1.0 and Spacecat/1.0 fetch pages
    • Last-Modified header on pages, or content fixes are skipped
    • CDN logs for agentic traffic: Adobe documents log forwarding for customer-managed CDNs (BYOCDN), so confirm how logs from AEM's managed CDN reach Brand Visibility
    • Each deployed fix counts against the license's 1,000 Optimizations a year
    Sow availability

    Not stated by Adobe. The paid Brand Visibility offer is assumed, because trial workspaces have tighter deployment limits.

    Sow prereqs
    • Brand Visibility license; users need the Adobe LLM Optimizer Users product profile (trial users: the LLMO Admin IMS group)
    • Site served by the AEM as a Cloud Service managed CDN (Fastly) as the outer CDN; your client's CDN in front needs its own routing
    • Robots.txt and bot rules that let AdobeEdgeOptimize/1.0 and Spacecat/1.0 fetch pages
    • Last-Modified header on pages, or content fixes are skipped
    • CDN logs for agentic traffic: Adobe documents log forwarding for customer-managed CDNs (BYOCDN), so how logs from AEM's managed CDN reach Brand Visibility is confirmed with Adobe before this service starts
    • Each deployed fix counts against the license's 1,000 Optimizations a year

    • A CJA data view that maps Page URL, Referring Domain, Country and Device Type, plus Page Views, Visits and Visitors (revenue and orders optional)
    • Acceptance that some Brand Visibility data is processed temporarily in the United States

    Original wording reviewed
    How

    Brand Concierge's built-in analytics dashboard is powered by Customer Journey Analytics and needs no CJA license; analyzing conversations with the rest of the customer journey needs a separately licensed CJA and Adobe's confirmation that the concierge dataset can be used there.

    Kind

    native

    Availability

    Built-in dashboard: generally available. Analysis in your client's own CJA: not documented by Adobe; confirm the data use with Adobe.

    Prereqs
    • A deployed concierge; the built-in dashboard needs no other setup and no CJA license (it runs on Brand Concierge's own reporting engine, limited to 2 concurrent and 100,000 monthly report requests)
    • For journey and revenue analysis: CJA licensed separately (Brand Concierge's license excludes other CJA use)
    • Adobe's written confirmation that the concierge dataset may be joined with your client's web or commerce data in a CJA connection (the product description limits Brand Concierge's data lake storage to Brand Concierge's analytical requirements); otherwise, concierge events sent through the client-side callback functions into your client's own data collection

    Original wording reviewed
    How

    The AEM Assets Integration for Commerce links approved AEM Assets to Commerce products by SKU, or by custom matching built in Adobe Developer App Builder, and syncs them into the catalog; merchandisers can also pick DAM assets inside the Commerce Admin. On Commerce on Cloud and on-premises it's an Adobe extension the partner installs; on Commerce as a Cloud Service it's configured in the Commerce Admin.

    Kind

    native

    Availability

    Not stated by Adobe; free for merchants who meet the licensing requirements, with setup that differs by Commerce deployment.

    Prereqs
    • Active Adobe Commerce, AEM Assets and AEM Dynamic Media licenses (on Commerce as a Cloud Service and Commerce Optimizer, the included Product Visuals powered by AEM Assets license is the alternative)
    • AEM Assets as a Cloud Service author environment in the same IMS organization as Commerce
    • Commerce on Cloud (PaaS) or on-premises: Adobe Commerce 2.4.5 or later and Adobe's aem-assets-integration extension, installed with Composer from repo.magento.com
    • Commerce on Cloud (PaaS) or on-premises: the Commerce Services Connector (API keys and data space), Adobe I/O Events for Commerce with RabbitMQ and cron (Adobe I/O modules installed on 2.4.5), and an OAuth integration created in the Commerce Admin
    • Commerce Optimizer: no Admin UI; Adobe Support configures the integration from the onboarding ticket
    • AEM release 2026.5.26309 or later for self-service setup (COMMERCE_INTEGRATION_ENABLED); earlier releases deploy the assets-commerce package through a Cloud Manager pipeline
    • Dynamic Media with OpenAPI activated (support ticket if the button is unavailable)
    • Approval metadata schema configured, and assets approved and tagged with SKUs; custom matching needs Adobe Developer App Builder code
    • IMS user permissions for the Asset Selector in the Commerce Admin

    • The reporting source chosen before launch; it cannot change after the activity goes live, and an activity reports to one source only
    • For CJA audiences in Target: a Real-Time CDP or Journey Optimizer entitlement for the Target destination, Target provisioned, and a Target-enabled datastream

    extension

    • Web SDK route (aem.live Target guide, no plugin): alloy.js in the site repository, Adobe's documented code in scripts.js, the IMS org ID and a datastream with Target enabled
    • Legacy at.js route, also on aem.live: Target client code and IMS org ID
    • Martech plugin route only: the aem-martech plugin (co-innovation per the One Adobe lab), Adobe Analytics, a datastream connected to Target and Analytics, and a Tags property with the Adobe Client Data Layer extension
    • Target turned on for the agreed pages, typically with a Target page metadata flag as aem.live recommends
    • Consent management platform connected (the boilerplate consent check declines consent by default; the plugin defaults consent to pending)
    • Optional, for authors: Experience Workspace Send to Adobe Target needs an Adobe Developer Console project with the Target API

    Original wording reviewed
    How

    Dynamic Media with OpenAPI lets Sites authors use approved assets from a remote AEM Assets environment in the Page Editor (remote assets in Content Fragments work on AEM 6.5, not on AEM as a Cloud Service); Adobe recommends it over the older Connected Assets.

    native

    Availability

    • AEM Assets as a Cloud Service and AEM Dynamic Media licenses
    • Applies when the DAM is a separate (remote) AEM environment
    • Dynamic Media with OpenAPI enabled, and the IMS Client ID issued, through an Adobe Support ticket
    • Cloud Manager variables ASSET_DELIVERY_REPOSITORY_ID and ASSET_DELIVERY_IMS_CLIENT on the Sites environment
    • Core Components 2.23.2 or later with Image v3; other and custom components need customization
    • HTTPS on every environment that uses remote assets
    • Sites authors with IMS access to the remote DAM
    • Smart crop is not among the basic modifiers Adobe lists for Dynamic Media Prime; confirm your client's Dynamic Media edition

    Original wording reviewed
    How

    CX Enterprise Coworker Chat runs inside Workfront within each user's permissions. It is read-only until a system admin turns on the Write MCP tools option, and Adobe says Coworker is not currently offered to health care, finance or some other industries.

    Kind

    native

    Availability

    Coworker Chat is generally available in Workfront, but Adobe says Coworker is not currently offered to health care, finance or some other industries.

    Prereqs
    • Workfront Standard license (any Workfront package)
    • CX Enterprise Coworker licensed through the Adobe account team; Adobe's support or professional services team configures Coworker, its Adobe app integrations and its governance and approval workflows
    • Write MCP tools option enabled in System Preferences by a Workfront admin before Coworker can change anything
    • Users need existing Workfront access to each object
    • Coworker is not currently offered to organizations in health care, finance or some other industries (Adobe's Coworker in Workfront page); confirm eligibility
    Sow prereqs
    • Workfront Standard license (any Workfront package)
    • CX Enterprise Coworker licensed through the Adobe account team; Adobe's support or professional services team configures Coworker, its Adobe app integrations and its governance and approval workflows
    • Write MCP tools option enabled in System Preferences by a Workfront admin before Coworker can change anything
    • Users need existing Workfront access to each object
    • Adobe confirms that Coworker is available to the Client's organization (Adobe's Coworker in Workfront page says it is not currently offered to organizations in health care, finance or some other industries)

    Method and limits

    The review covers sow/canvas/catalog.json and the CATALOG in sow/index.html at the pinned commit. Services were matched by ID, with original SOW scope, deliverables, acceptance criteria, assumptions and scope bands included where present. Connection sources and flow sources were deduplicated by URL but assessed against each distinct claim.

    The review asks whether the source supports the material work, the product and deployment model, the direction of an integration, and any important prerequisites or release restrictions. Existing partner-managed and tenant-confirmation qualifications count. Ordinary workshops, training, review cadence and quantity limits are not rejected merely because Adobe does not prescribe them.

    VerdictMeaning
    Direct supportThe current source set supports the material product capability and service fit. Partner quantities, hours and delivery methods still require engagement-specific scoping.
    Partial supportThe current source set supports a meaningful portion, but another material part, limitation or prerequisite needs a better citation or clearer wording.
    Background onlyThe linked material concerns the product or adjacent capability but does not substantiate the core work as described.
    No supporting source foundNo adequate attached or researched support was recorded. Generic partner advisory work can still be valid without an Adobe capability claim.
    Unable to verifyThe evidence could not be adequately retrieved or resolved; no positive or negative capability conclusion is certified.

    High priority means material capability/dependency ambiguity or unresolved evidence that could affect the SOW. Medium priority means a substantive citation or scope correction. Low priority means a narrower provenance or navigation improvement. These priorities are review judgments, not Adobe product ratings.

    This is a documentation audit. It does not execute integrations in a customer tenant, confirm a customer's contract, validate effort estimates, or certify regulatory compliance. It records the public evidence retrieved for this snapshot. Adobe pages can change after the review, and a deployed copy of the generator may differ from the repository snapshot.

    Keeping the citations defensible

    For each service, retain the specific claim, primary source, section, supporting sources, prerequisites and last review date. Give compound services enough sources to cover their distinct promises. Keep a small set of primary links on the service card and make supporting evidence available in a reference detail view. Review a service's evidence whenever its scope, product dependency or source page changes.

    Use an automated link check for retrieval and redirects, followed by a content review for substantive claims. A successful request alone cannot show that the destination supports the service. Treat unresolved evidence as a visible exception, and keep estimates and partner delivery choices separate from vendor-supported capabilities.

    Audit completed for the stated snapshot. All 278 records have a verdict. The complete machine-readable record and workbook accompany this report. Proposed corrections have not been applied to the generator.
